title: SSD Wear Leveling and Health
exclusions: This use case covers the standard controller-level NVMe SMART/Health Information log on Linux hosts with directly visible NVMe controllers. It does not cover SATA/SAS SMART, drives hidden behind a RAID controller, vendor-specific log pages, per-namespace health where the controller does not support it, or prediction of a failure date. `Percentage Used` is not a remaining-life percentage or a declaration that a device has failed; 100 means the vendor-estimated endurance has been consumed and the value may exceed 100. Warranty and replacement decisions must use the exact drive model's current vendor documentation, workload risk, redundancy, and maintenance policy.
evidence: When deployed, retain the `nvme_ssd_endurance_health` saved-search definition, a result export containing `last_seen`, `host`, `device`, `serial_number`, `percentage_used`, spare values, warning bitmask, media-error delta, severity, and trigger reason, plus the matching one-line collector JSON and a time-correlated `nvme smart-log -o json` capture from the host. These artifacts demonstrate what the controller reported and how the search classified it; they do not prove remaining service life.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In a test index using sourcetype `linux:nvme:smart`, load normalized JSON for three distinct serial numbers within the 20-minute search window. Device A has `collection_status="ok"`, `critical_warning=0`, `percentage_used=80`, `available_spare=100`, `available_spare_threshold=10`, and unchanged `media_errors=0`; expect one warning row with reason `planning threshold reached`. Device B has `percentage_used=20`, `available_spare=9`, `available_spare_threshold=10`; expect one critical row for spare below the controller threshold. For Device C, load an earlier event with `media_errors=4` and a later event with `media_errors=5`; expect one critical row with `media_errors_delta=1`. Also verify that `percentage_used=100` and any nonzero `critical_warning` independently produce critical rows.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Load two events five minutes apart for one test serial with `collection_status="ok"`, `critical_warning=0`, `percentage_used=79`, `available_spare=10`, `available_spare_threshold=10`, and `media_errors=7` in both events. The search must return zero rows: equality at the spare threshold is not the NVMe-defined below-threshold condition, a historical but unchanged media-error counter is not a new error, and 79 is below the local 80% planning threshold. Separately load `collection_status="error"` with null health fields and confirm it is excluded from this health alert and appears in the collection-health check described in Step 3.

dataSources: A Linux scripted input runs `nvme smart-log -o json` once per `/sys/class/nvme/nvmeN` controller every 300 seconds and emits one normalized JSON event per controller. `index=os` is a deployment choice and `sourcetype=linux:nvme:smart` is a local convention, not a vendor or CIM sourcetype. Required extracted fields are `device`, `serial_number`, `model`, `collection_status`, `critical_warning`, `available_spare`, `available_spare_threshold`, `percentage_used`, `data_units_written`, `media_errors`, `power_on_hours`, and `collection_epoch`. A Universal Forwarder scripted input is sufficient; Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833) is optional for adjacent host telemetry and does not supply this NVMe collector.
app: A private deployment app (for example `TA_linux_nvme_health`) containing the scripted input and JSON search-time extraction, executed by a Splunk Universal Forwarder. No product-specific Splunkbase add-on is required; Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833) is optional and is not the source of `nvme smart-log` fields.
spl:
index=os sourcetype="linux:nvme:smart" collection_status="ok" earliest=-20m@m
| eval percentage_used=tonumber(percentage_used), available_spare=tonumber(available_spare), available_spare_threshold=tonumber(available_spare_threshold), critical_warning=tonumber(critical_warning), media_errors=tonumber(media_errors), data_units_written=tonumber(data_units_written)
| where isnotnull(percentage_used) AND isnotnull(available_spare) AND isnotnull(available_spare_threshold) AND isnotnull(critical_warning) AND isnotnull(media_errors)
| stats latest(_time) as last_seen latest(model) as model latest(firmware_revision) as firmware_revision latest(percentage_used) as percentage_used latest(available_spare) as available_spare latest(available_spare_threshold) as available_spare_threshold latest(critical_warning) as critical_warning earliest(media_errors) as media_errors_first latest(media_errors) as media_errors_latest latest(data_units_written) as data_units_written by host device serial_number
| eval media_errors_delta=if(media_errors_latest>=media_errors_first, media_errors_latest-media_errors_first, 0), host_written_tb=round(data_units_written*512000/1000000000000, 2)
| eval severity=case(critical_warning>0, "critical", available_spare<available_spare_threshold, "critical", media_errors_delta>0, "critical", percentage_used>=100, "critical", percentage_used>=80, "warning", true(), "normal")
| eval trigger_reason=case(critical_warning>0, "NVMe critical-warning bitmask is nonzero", available_spare<available_spare_threshold, "available spare is below controller threshold", media_errors_delta>0, "media/data-integrity error counter increased", percentage_used>=100, "vendor-estimated endurance consumed", percentage_used>=80, "local endurance-planning threshold reached")
| where severity!="normal"
| convert ctime(last_seen)
| table last_seen host device serial_number model firmware_revision percentage_used available_spare available_spare_threshold critical_warning media_errors_latest media_errors_delta host_written_tb severity trigger_reason
| sort 0 severity -percentage_used
description: Tracks the latest standard NVMe SMART/Health sample per Linux host, controller device, and serial number over a 20-minute window. A result is produced when the controller reports any critical-warning bit, available spare below its own threshold, a new media/data-integrity error, vendor-estimated endurance consumption of at least 100%, or the local 80% replacement-planning threshold.
value: Storage teams gain an auditable, model-aware queue for planned SSD replacement before endurance limits or controller health warnings become an unplanned service event. Separating device-defined critical conditions from the tunable 80% planning signal avoids treating a vendor estimate as a universal failure prediction and helps procurement lead time match actual fleet risk.
implementation: Deploy a least-privilege Python 3 scripted input that normalizes `nvme-cli` JSON once per controller every five minutes, configure JSON field extraction, then schedule the SPL every five minutes over 20 minutes. Treat 80% as a local planning threshold, 100% as estimated endurance consumed rather than failure, and compare available spare with the controller's own threshold.
visualization: Use a table keyed by `host`, `device`, and `serial_number` with severity and trigger reason; a fleet distribution chart of `percentage_used` in 10-point bands; a timechart of `percentage_used` and decimal `host_written_tb` per serial; and collection-health single values for controllers with missing or stale samples. Label `percentage_used` as endurance consumed (%) and `available_spare` as remaining normalized spare (%); never label either as guaranteed life remaining.

references.title: NVM Express Base Specification, Revision 2.3 — SMART / Health Information Log
Solidigm SSD Data Center Family SMART Attributes
Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (optional; Splunkbase 833)

knownFalsePositives:
1. **fio or vendor burn-in qualification** — A planned endurance test can legitimately push `percentage_used` through 80 or add media errors on a sacrificial device. Confirm the serial number against the lab job and suppress only that serial with a time-bound maintenance exception.

2. **NVMe firmware activation or controller recalibration** — Firmware can revise a vendor-specific endurance estimate or leave a warning asserted until the documented reset/power-cycle sequence completes. Compare the indexed JSON with a fresh `nvme smart-log -o json` result and the model-specific vendor release notes; do not suppress a read-only or reliability-degraded warning merely because firmware changed.

3. **Drive replacement on a reused Linux controller path** — If a replacement has a blank or duplicated serial, events for the old and new drive can share `/dev/nvmeN` and create a misleading counter delta. Require serial-bearing inventory before paging, verify `/sys/class/nvme/<device>/serial`, and filter the SPL for the affected host/device only until identity is corrected.

4. **Approved operation beyond the local 80% planning point** — A redundant lab, cache, or decommissioning workload may intentionally retain a healthy device after the warning threshold. Record owner, reason, and expiry in an optional local `nvme_health_exceptions.csv` lookup keyed by `host` and `serial_number`; an exception may suppress the 80% planning reason but must not suppress nonzero critical warnings, spare-below-threshold, new media errors, or `percentage_used>=100` without storage-owner review.

5. **Synthetic control-test events** — Test JSON in the production index matches real health fields by design. Run tests in a restricted test index where possible; otherwise tag them with a locally added `test_event=true` field and add an explicit `test_event!=true` filter to the production saved search after proving the control test separately.
reviewer: Cursor documentation review; primary-source editorial review only, no runtime or SME validation
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

Use this control only for Linux hosts where each NVMe controller is visible as `/dev/nvmeN`; the default `nvme smart-log` request is controller-global, not proof of per-namespace health. Install a supported `nvme-cli` package and system Python 3 because the Universal Forwarder does not bundle Python. The forwarder service account needs enough permission to open the NVMe controller character devices and execute the binary, but it does not need shell login or write access to storage. Prefer a narrowly scoped OS group and a reviewed udev rule for `SUBSYSTEM=="nvme"` controller devices over unrestricted sudo or running the forwarder as root. Confirm manually, as that service account, that `/usr/sbin/nvme smart-log -o json /dev/nvme0` succeeds. Create the deployment-selected `index=os` (or replace it consistently), and package the collector in a private app such as `TA_linux_nvme_health`; `sourcetype=linux:nvme:smart` is this use case's local convention. Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833) may provide surrounding CPU and filesystem context, but it neither installs `nvme-cli` nor creates these fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Place the `scriptExample` body at `TA_linux_nvme_health/bin/collect_nvme_smart.py`, make it executable, and test it under the forwarder account. It enumerates controller entries matching `/sys/class/nvme/nvmeN`, calls the standard SMART/Health log once per controller, accepts both descriptive nvme-cli v1 names (`percentage_used`, `available_spare`, `available_spare_threshold`) and v2-style short names (`percent_used`, `avail_spare`, `spare_thresh`), and emits one compact JSON object per controller. A 300-second interval normally yields 288 events per controller per day. The collector emits `collection_status="error"` instead of inventing zero values when a command, permission, timeout, or JSON parse fails.

Configure `local/inputs.conf` in the private app:

```ini
[script://./bin/collect_nvme_smart.py]
disabled = 0
interval = 300
index = os
sourcetype = linux:nvme:smart
source = nvme_smart_log
```

Configure search-time extraction in the app delivered to search heads (and line handling where parsing occurs):

```ini
[linux:nvme:smart]
SHOULD_LINEMERGE = false
LINE_BREAKER = ([\r\n]+)
TRUNCATE = 0
CHARSET = UTF-8
KV_MODE = json
```

Do not combine `KV_MODE=json` with `INDEXED_EXTRACTIONS=JSON`, which would duplicate fields. After restart or deployment reload, inspect `index=os sourcetype="linux:nvme:smart" | head 20 | fieldsummary`. For every `collection_status=ok` event, require numeric `critical_warning`, `available_spare`, `available_spare_threshold`, `percentage_used`, `data_units_written`, `media_errors`, and `power_on_hours`, plus nonblank `device` and `serial_number`. `percentage_used` and both spare fields are integer percentage points. `critical_warning` is a bitmask, not a count. `media_errors` is a lifetime cumulative count. One Data Unit Written represents 1,000 units of 512 bytes, so the SPL converts one raw unit to 512,000 bytes and reports decimal TB; it is host data written, not NAND writes and not automatically the model's rated TBW.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Save the `spl` field as `nvme_ssd_endurance_health`, schedule it every five minutes, and search the previous 20 minutes so a delayed poll does not immediately hide a controller. Trigger once per result and suppress repeated actions by `host,device,serial_number,severity` for an operationally chosen period; four hours is a reasonable starting point for warning reminders, while critical results should follow the storage incident policy. Preserve the full result in the ticket rather than sending only the severity.

```spl
index=os sourcetype="linux:nvme:smart" collection_status="ok" earliest=-20m@m
| eval percentage_used=tonumber(percentage_used), available_spare=tonumber(available_spare), available_spare_threshold=tonumber(available_spare_threshold), critical_warning=tonumber(critical_warning), media_errors=tonumber(media_errors), data_units_written=tonumber(data_units_written)
| where isnotnull(percentage_used) AND isnotnull(available_spare) AND isnotnull(available_spare_threshold) AND isnotnull(critical_warning) AND isnotnull(media_errors)
| stats latest(_time) as last_seen latest(model) as model latest(firmware_revision) as firmware_revision latest(percentage_used) as percentage_used latest(available_spare) as available_spare latest(available_spare_threshold) as available_spare_threshold latest(critical_warning) as critical_warning earliest(media_errors) as media_errors_first latest(media_errors) as media_errors_latest latest(data_units_written) as data_units_written by host device serial_number
| eval media_errors_delta=if(media_errors_latest>=media_errors_first, media_errors_latest-media_errors_first, 0), host_written_tb=round(data_units_written*512000/1000000000000, 2)
| eval severity=case(critical_warning>0, "critical", available_spare<available_spare_threshold, "critical", media_errors_delta>0, "critical", percentage_used>=100, "critical", percentage_used>=80, "warning", true(), "normal")
| eval trigger_reason=case(critical_warning>0, "NVMe critical-warning bitmask is nonzero", available_spare<available_spare_threshold, "available spare is below controller threshold", media_errors_delta>0, "media/data-integrity error counter increased", percentage_used>=100, "vendor-estimated endurance consumed", percentage_used>=80, "local endurance-planning threshold reached")
| where severity!="normal"
```

Understanding this SPL: `latest()` selects the newest health value by event time for each physical identity, while `earliest(media_errors)` and `latest(media_errors)` detect a counter increase without paging merely because a controller has historical errors. A counter decrease is treated as zero delta because it usually means reset or replacement and needs identity review, not a fabricated negative count. The NVMe standard says Available Spare must fall below the controller's Available Spare Threshold, so equality does not fire and there is no universal 5% rule. `Percentage Used` is a vendor-specific estimate of endurance consumed: 100 means estimated endurance has been consumed, not that failure is certain; values may continue above 100 and saturate at 255. The 80% arm is therefore an explicit local planning policy, not an NVMe-mandated warning. Tune it from model-specific endurance guidance, procurement lead time, redundancy, workload criticality, and observed write rate.

Step 3 — Validate fields, semantics, and control behavior

For two controllers from different models, compare the indexed event with a command captured at the same time: `nvme smart-log -o json /dev/nvmeN`. Match serial, warning bitmask, percentage used, spare and threshold, media errors, data units written, and power-on hours. Read the exact model string and serial from `/sys/class/nvme/nvmeN/{model,serial}` to prove that Linux controller numbering has not been mistaken for identity. Check the model's vendor datasheet or support page before interpreting decimal host-written TB as warranty consumption; rated TBW and vendor-specific NAND-write counters are not standardized by this collector.

Execute both `controlTest` scenarios in a test index and substitute that index in a copy of the saved search. The positive set must exercise each independent arm. The negative set deliberately uses `available_spare=available_spare_threshold`, an unchanged nonzero media-error count, and `percentage_used=79`; zero rows proves the boundary and delta semantics. Documentation review does not constitute execution, so retain actual test output only after an operator runs it.

Create a separate collection-health panel or alert:

```spl
index=os sourcetype="linux:nvme:smart" earliest=-20m@m
| stats latest(_time) as last_seen latest(collection_status) as collection_status latest(collector_error) as collector_error by host device
| where collection_status!="ok" OR last_seen<relative_time(now(), "-10m")
```

Also chart `timechart span=5m count by host` for 24 hours and compare distinct serial counts with `ls /sys/class/nvme/` on sampled hosts. Health SPL cannot protect a controller that silently stopped reporting.

Step 4 — Operationalize evidence and response

Build a fleet table with the exact units in `visualization`; place collection health beside wear health so missing data is visible. Give search access only to storage/platform responders and administrators authorized for `index=os`, because serial numbers and firmware inventory may be operationally sensitive. The runbook should first confirm the live log and serial, decode the nonzero critical-warning bitmask with the NVMe specification or model documentation, inspect redundancy and current I/O errors, then open a replacement or vendor case. Escalate read-only, reliability-degraded, spare-below-threshold, and newly increasing media-error conditions promptly. For an 80% planning row, estimate lead time and trend rather than declaring imminent failure. Preserve the saved-search configuration, result row, raw normalized event, live command capture, ticket, and disposition as the evidence package.

Step 5 — Troubleshoot product-specific failures

No controller events: verify `nvme-cli` exists in the scripted input's PATH, Python 3 exists on the host, the glob finds `/sys/class/nvme/nvmeN`, and the forwarder account can open `/dev/nvmeN`. Script stderr is written to `splunkd.log`; use the collector's `collection_status` event for the user-facing reason. Do not solve an ioctl permission error with blanket passwordless sudo.

Fields are null: confirm the raw event is one complete JSON object and that `KV_MODE=json` is deployed to the search tier. nvme-cli output format versions can rename fields; the collector intentionally normalizes the known long and short names. Treat an unknown schema as `collection_status="error"` and update the normalization only after checking the installed nvme-cli documentation.

Percentage appears stuck: the standard permits `Percentage Used` to update once per power-on hour while the controller is awake, so a five-minute flat line is expected. Do not manufacture fractional precision or infer exact remaining days from it.

Media-error alert after a swap: compare serial numbers and power-on hours. A reused `/dev/nvmeN` path is not a durable identity; correct missing/duplicate serial extraction before suppressing the alert.

Written TB disagrees with a vendor tool: confirm that the comparison is host writes, not NAND writes. The standard Data Units Written conversion is 512,000 bytes per raw unit; write amplification and vendor log pages can make NAND-write totals larger. Use the product-specific endurance source for replacement or warranty decisions.
grandmaExplanation: We watch how much of each fast storage drive's expected working life has been used and whether the drive reports shrinking spare capacity or new internal errors. This gives the team time to check and replace a drive deliberately instead of assuming a percentage is a guaranteed failure date.
mitreAttack: N/A (operational hardware health monitoring; no security behavior is asserted)
hardware: Linux hosts with NVMe controllers directly exposed through `/dev/nvmeN`; model-specific endurance ratings and vendor log pages must be evaluated separately.
